result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers bury a coherent token set under long lists of additions, which works against the rubric's call for few changes and brevity. Answer A is shorter, but it asserts that contrast is solid before admitting the ratios were hand-estimated, and it calls a z-index scale and --radius-lg cheap to add now. Answer B is longer, but it names why the set is coherent, flags its contrast estimates up front, and pushes back on speculative growth: no filling in spacing steps, --radius-lg only when needed, no raw color ramp yet. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers affirm the set is sound but then pile on many additions (focus, strong border, status tints, fonts, touch targets, motion, and more). Neither stays short, though both avoid renaming tokens or reprinting the file. A edges ahead: it flags its contrast estimates as approximate up front, explicitly warns against filling scale gaps or adding a primitive ramp, and adds fewer speculative tokens. B adds more speculative scales (text-xs, z-index, radius-lg, action-active, row hover/selected), states a WCAG failure and an unverified hex value as fact, and only hedges about contrast at the end.
